title: Timbisha jar-shaped basket
material: willow, bulrush, yucca root; coiled (3 rods)
openAction: Pass the tag through the narrow mouth
fact: Cleveland identifies a Timbisha (Panamint) Shoshone coiled basket. It traces some lower woven figures to neighboring Yokuts basketry.
limit: The two communities’ connections help place the design. They leave the maker and the basket’s particular journeys open.
alt: Rounded woven basket with inward-curving shoulders and dark figures around its lower wall.

title: Skokomish storage basket
material: twined
openAction: Lift the model cover clear of the twining
fact: Cleveland describes the large storage basket as twined and places it with Skokomish basketry around 1900.
limit: The entry identifies weaving and scale. Any trial cover belongs to the Ferry model.
alt: Tall woven storage basket with a broad opening and decorated sides.

title: Small Pomo gift basket
place: Pomo, Lytton Springs, Alexander Valley, California
material: Bulrush, Sedge; Coiled (3 rods)
openAction: Draw the little tag out by its cord
fact: The collection dates the small coiled bulrush and sedge piece to 1895 and proposes that baskets like it were made for an outside market.
limit: The proposal stops short of identifying this individual basket’s buyer or recipient.
alt: Small round basket with a dark pattern and a wide mouth against a plain backdrop.

title: Lakota soft-hide bag
material: Native-tanned hide, glass beads, dyed horsehair, tin cones, sinew thread
openAction: Open the folded hide flap on the practice bag
fact: The collection records a soft hide bag with glass beads and tin cones and describes how bags of this type stored personal items and travelled beside a saddle.
limit: The record gives a documented role for bags of this form. It leaves this individual bag’s exact load and route unknown.
alt: Decorated rectangular hide bag with beading and fringe.

title: Mindanao handled container
material: Cast brass with silver inlays, weave fabric (handle), glass beads
openAction: Bring the case through the model handle loop
fact: Cleveland identifies a cast brass container with silver inlays and a woven, beaded handle, and gives the Maranao attribution as most likely.
limit: The catalogue distinguishes its attribution from a comparison of the strap with Bagobo beadwork.
alt: Rectangular brass container with silver decoration and a colorful beaded handle.

title: Saryk woven bag face
material: Wool, silk, cotton; 252 symmetrical rug knots per square inch
openAction: Lift the separately marked practice flap
fact: Cleveland holds the Saryk bag face. It identifies wool, silk and cotton on the woven front and describes suspended storage bags in comparable use.
limit: This accession preserves the front. The ferry’s sleeve and closure are stand-ins.
alt: Broad dark red woven panel with repeating lobed motifs.

title: Lacquered chrysanthemum gourd basket
material: gourd; lacquered and painted with gesso, color, and gold pigments
openAction: Reach past the curved wall
fact: Cleveland describes carving and lacquering a gourd. It records a signature underneath and attributes the artist role to Ogata Kōrin.
limit: The signature and catalogue attribution guide the source note. Ferry handling is a new experiment.
alt: Rounded carved basket with pale chrysanthemum relief on a green ground.

title: Japanese writing box with a Penglai scene
material: lacquer
openAction: Raise the painted cover before reading
fact: Cleveland describes a Japanese portable writing box whose lacquer cover uses a Chinese image of Mount Penglai. It notes a place for an ink stone inside.
limit: A motif can travel independently of a box. The cover supplies no trip record for this object.
alt: Lacquer writing box with a decorated landscape on the lid.

title: English waist-hung agate case
material: gray agate mounted in gilt metal
openAction: Unhook the miniature case from its loop
fact: Cleveland identifies an agate case mounted in gilt metal and an ornate clasp for carrying this kind of small case at the waist.
limit: The object shows how a case can be carried. Its individual wearer and contents remain open.
alt: Agate case with gilt mount attached to a decorative hanging clasp.

title: English fitted vanity case
material: gold, agate, interior fitted with gold-mounted implements, mirror
openAction: Move one fitted tool before lifting the tag
fact: Cleveland describes a gold and agate case fitted with small gold-mounted implements and a mirror.
limit: The fitted interior tells a reader what sits where. It cannot establish the owner’s journeys or conditions of use.
alt: Opened fitted case with a mirror and small gold-colored implements.

title: Joseon stamped floral tea caddy
catalogueTitle: Tea Caddy with Stamped Floral Decoration
material: glazed stoneware with stamped and incised inlaid white slip decoration
openAction: Lift the tag straight out past the stoneware rim
fact: Cleveland identifies glazed stoneware with stamped and inlaid decoration and proposes a later use among Japanese powdered-tea drinkers.
limit: The proposed trade history and use remain possibilities. The earlier catalogue date is for the vessel.
alt: Small glazed stoneware vessel with pale stamped floral decoration.

title: Meissen porcelain tea caddy
material: porcelain
openAction: Lift the fitted top before presenting the card
fact: Cleveland credits the Meissen Porcelain Factory for the small porcelain tea caddy dated around 1735.
limit: The factory credit identifies manufacture. The object gives no ferry weather or known load.
alt: Small decorated porcelain tea caddy with a narrow top.

title: Samuel Herbert and Company cake basket
material: Silver
openAction: Release the trial thread from the basket rim
fact: Cleveland names Samuel Herbert and Company as maker of the dated silver cake basket and relates its form to formal serving.
limit: A serving form can keep food visible. An internal paper sleeve in this session is a stand-in.
alt: Shallow silver cake basket with a decorative edge and raised handle.

title: Chancay weaving basket and contents
material: Cane, shell, bone, fiber, camelid hair, wood, pigment, metal, stone
openAction: Separate the loose practice tag from the tool group
fact: The Met records one parent accession with a cane basket and a separately numbered group of weaving materials and implements.
limit: A lid or travel strap is absent from the catalogue evidence used here. The practice cover is fictional.
alt: A narrow woven basket and a group of individually arranged weaving objects.

title: Middle Niger miniature basket (?)
material: Copper alloy

people.name: Middle Niger artist
people.role: Unnamed artist attribution in the catalogue

openAction: Retrieve the tag from the enlarged model opening
fact: The Met labels the small copper-alloy piece Miniature Basket (?) and credits a Middle Niger artist without an individual name.
limit: The question mark is part of the catalogue title. The enlarged trial model leaves the original function open.
alt: Small copper-alloy object with the outline of a miniature basket.

title: Mary Tecuyas’s cooking basket
material: Cladium root, yucca root, sumac, bracken fern root on bundle foundation
openAction: Unclip the tag from the copy’s bowl-shaped rim
fact: The Met credits Mary Tecuyas for this cooking basket and lists roots and sumac worked on a bundle foundation.
limit: Cooking is the documented use. The practice ferry parcel borrows its shape alone.
alt: Broad shallow basket with a patterned interior and circular rim.

title: Tiwanaku plant-fiber basket
material: Plant fiber
openAction: Pull the tag past the model basket’s mouth
fact: The Met identifies the compact basket as plant fiber and gives a wide sixth- to eleventh-century date range.
limit: The surviving form and range leave its contents, its individual maker, and its particular trips undetermined.
alt: Compact woven basket with its sides tapering toward the base.

title: Japanese square calligraphy paper box
catalogueTitle: Basketry Box for Square Calligraphy Paper (Shikishibako) with Paulownia
material: Lacquered bamboo basketry with gold hiramaki-e
openAction: Slide the note clear of the square practice sheets
fact: The Met identifies a lacquered bamboo basketry box for square calligraphy paper, with gold paulownia decoration.
limit: The recorded intended type of paper leaves the identity of the person who packed it open.
alt: Shallow square lacquered basketry box with gold decoration.

title: Japanese portable picnic set
material: Lacquered wood with gold, silver, red togidashimaki-e, hiramaki-e on black and nashiji lacquer ground
openAction: Choose the tray nearest the lid mark and lift it
fact: The Met records a portable picnic set with lacquered wooden fittings across one accession group from the second half of the nineteenth century.
limit: A set can travel together while containing separately identified parts. Its packing order for a specific occasion remains unknown.
alt: Tall lacquered picnic carrier with fitted, decorated compartments.

title: Chinese lotus traveling box
material: Polychromatic lacquer, leather, wood, and iron damascened with gold
openAction: Separate the outside claim slip from the cover
fact: The Met identifies an early fifteenth-century traveling box and records lacquer, leather, wood and iron damascened with gold.
limit: Travel is in the catalogue title. The route of a particular journey remains unidentified.
alt: Lidded traveling box with a dark ground and lotus scroll decoration.

title: Urbino maiolica writing case
material: Maiolica (tin-glazed earthenware)
openAction: Lift one part before finding the model label
fact: The Met catalogs the late sixteenth-century writing case as maiolica and groups its parts under one accession.
limit: The grouped object record cannot tell us who opened it or how quickly they worked.
alt: Low, horizontal decorated ceramic writing case.

title: Traveling case catalogued with Bartholomew Newsam
material: Leather and brass, partly gilded
openAction: Open the copy gently to reach the inner tag
fact: The Met credits Bartholomew Newsam as maker in the traveling-case record and identifies leather and partly gilded brass.
limit: The credit belongs with this record. The simulation supplies its own tag and handling conditions.
alt: Short leather traveling case with applied metallic fittings.

title: American leather satchel
material: leather, metal
openAction: Open the copy’s practice hardware and unfold the tag
fact: The Met dates this American leather and metal satchel to the middle of the nineteenth century and gives the components the same parent accession.
limit: A catalogued satchel can model carrying. The record leaves its owner’s route and load unrecorded.
alt: Brown leather satchel with metal hardware and a narrow handle.

title: Oneida lidded ash basket
material: Ash splint, wood, pigment
openAction: Open the broad copy lid and hold it while reading
fact: The Met lists ash splint, wood and pigment for this broad Oneida basket and identifies the lid within the accession.
limit: A lid is positively recorded here. What it covered on any given day remains open.
alt: Broad lidded basket woven in light ash splints with darker marks.

title: Lidded basket attributed to Haudenosaunee makers
place: Haudenosaunee, possibly Seneca or Onondaga, New York, United States
material: Ash splint, wood, pigment
openAction: Lift the lid without tearing the separate attribution slip
fact: The Met identifies the ash basket and lid as Haudenosaunee and gives Seneca or Onondaga as possible closer attributions.
limit: Keep the two possible affiliations on the tag until a record can support a narrower attribution.
alt: Lidded basket with light woven splints and a patterned band.

title: Wide basket possibly made by Passamaquoddy makers
material: Ash splint, wood, pigment
openAction: Keep the uncertain maker note clipped beneath the lid
fact: The Met records a wide lidded storage basket in ash splint and lists the Passamaquoddy attribution as uncertain.
limit: The documented lid and the qualified attribution have different levels of certainty. Keep both readable.
alt: Wide lidded woven basket with a low profile.

title: Beaded bag from Quebec or the Canadian Maritimes
place: Mi’kmaq or Haudenosaunee, Quebec or the Canadian Maritimes
material: Wool, cotton, silk, glass, brass
openAction: Unfold the removable cloth sleeve to read its two possible names
fact: The Met names Mi’kmaq and Haudenosaunee as possibilities and lists glass beads, brass and several textile fibers.
limit: The possible communities are alternatives in this record. A shared ferry test cannot settle the maker.
alt: Small decorated textile bag with a beaded design and metal accents.

title: Pomo diagonally twined carrying basket
material: Willow shoot foundation, sedge root warp, redbud shoot weft, coiled-on oak rim rod and split wild grape vine rim wrap
openAction: Set the tag clear of the copy’s rim wrap
fact: The Met records diagonal twining and distinguishes willow foundation, sedge warp, redbud weft and a separate rim wrap.
limit: The construction identifies where the model can hold a tag. Its results cannot establish that past carriers clipped papers there.
alt: Tall diagonally twined carrying basket with a broad mouth and wrapped rim.

title: Apache storage basket
material: Willow shoots, devil's claw, and yucca root
openAction: Draw the tag up from the practice liner
fact: The Met locates this Apache storage basket in New Mexico and lists willow shoots, devil’s claw and yucca root.
limit: The broad Apache attribution leaves the individual maker and any closer community identification open.
alt: Tall round woven basket with broad repeating dark patterned bands.

title: Royal Porcelain Manufactory caddy
material: Hard-paste porcelain
openAction: Lift the small hard-paste copy cap
fact: The Met identifies the Royal Porcelain Manufactory and records hard-paste porcelain for the nineteenth-century caddy.
limit: The factory name identifies production. A particular owner or caddy load remains unrecorded here.
alt: Small decorated hard-paste porcelain caddy with a fitted top.

title: Worcester covered dessert basket
material: Soft-paste porcelain
openAction: Set the cover beside the base and take out the slip
fact: The Met identifies Worcester factory soft-paste porcelain and gives separate measurements for basket and cover.
limit: The cover is part of this documented object. The pull order and time are properties of the ferry’s trial.
alt: Decorative porcelain dessert basket with a separate fitted cover.

title: Philadelphia openwork fruit basket
material: Soft-paste porcelain with underglaze blue decoration
openAction: Release the tag from the practice basket’s opening
fact: The Met credits the American China Manufactory with making the openwork basket in soft-paste porcelain with underglaze blue decoration.
limit: The rim can guide clipping a trial tag. The object cannot tell a reader how such a tag would have fared.
alt: Small white openwork porcelain fruit basket with blue decoration.

title: Browne and Seal silver tea caddy
material: Silver
openAction: Lift the tag from the fitted practice slot
fact: The Met credits Browne and Seal and records separate body and base dimensions for the silver tea caddy.
limit: Those measurements support a fitting model. The tag stock and spray are new.
alt: Small silver caddy rising from a low rectangular base.

title: Muhammad Isma’il Isfahani mirror case and satin pouch
catalogueTitle: Mirror Case Depicting the Meeting of Nasir al-Din Mirza and Tsar Nicholas I in Erivan and Satin Pouch
material: a) Pasteboard, opaque color, watercolor, gold under a lacquer varnish b) Satin pouch with metal wrapped embroidery
feature: case in a separate satin pouch
openAction: Withdraw the case from the pouch before opening the slip
fact: The Met credits Muhammad Isma’il Isfahani, records 1271 AH / 1854 CE, and identifies a painted mirror case with a separate embroidered satin pouch.
limit: The painted meeting helps name the image. It leaves the original case’s own departure and arrival open.
alt: Painted lacquered mirror case alongside its separate embroidered satin pouch.

title: Lukutin and Fabergé lacquer box
material: lacquer, papier-mâché, gold, diamonds
openAction: Lift the shallow lip without reading the gold surface as a name
fact: Cleveland lists the House of Fabergé as maker and Factory N. Lukutin as workmaster. The factory produced the red lacquer box with gold patterns and diamond inlays.
limit: Keep the workshop and manufacturer roles distinct. Decoration alone gives no individual carrier or original contents.
alt: Shallow box with a deep red surface and fine gold decoration.

title: English writing case attributed to James Cox
material: agate, gold and diamond. mounted with 18 KT gold cagework
openAction: Lift the practice case from its cage before taking the slip
fact: Cleveland identifies agate, gold and diamond in the case. It assigns the artist role to James Cox as an attribution.
limit: The writing-case type tells how to describe it. The individual artist credit remains qualified.
alt: Small agate case held within decorative gold cagework.
